title: fuel-component separation and model exploration
summary: The [component definitions](task-f01.qmd#tbl-fuel-component-dictionary) separate vegetation components and pre-PCT litter/duff, omitting post-PCT forest-floor estimates. The [executable analytical sequence](task-f01.qmd#publication-execution) integrates derivation, exploration, candidate-fitting code, and complete CSV evidence; shared helpers are defined inline and saved for later tasks. The [model-review register](task-f01.qmd#rendered-provisional-model-review-register) reports provisional AIC leaders, not final selections. Prediction, inference, and display decisions belong to [RD04](task-rd04.qmd#rd04-inference-review); the task pages own calculation order and selective recomputation. Runs solely in the locked publication environment from committed thesis exports; current outputs and in-stage computational checks define the workflow. Quarto can recompute this whole task independently or render its saved evidence.

title: fuel phase and PCT display
target: Nine-panel figure, estimates table, and CSV
summary: The [nine-panel inventory](task-rd04.qmd#completed-output) reports phase-specific mean fuel loads and a matched woody contrast. The [inference review](task-rd04.qmd#rd04-inference-review) distinguishes model changes, random-effect integration, and unmatched thesis component definitions. The [accepted supplementary table](task-rd04.qmd#fuel-companion-table) presents all 60 estimates from the canonical CSV. Woody change uses the joint phase model and its pre/post covariance. Saved computational checks support the implementation; model adequacy and the RT03 narrative remain under review. F01 supplies the provisional fitted models. RD04 can render saved results or recompute from those fits in the locked publication environment.

title: regeneration basal area display
status: Completed - redwood treatment-dependent zeros and publication displays accepted
target: RW/TO Results figure and all-species supplement table
summary: RD02 is complete. The [selected models](task-rd02.qmd#rd02-selected-models) retain four separate hurdle-Gamma fits with treatment and site/macro-plot intercepts in the positive component. Redwood now includes treatment in its zero component; the other categories retain constant zero probabilities. The [zero-process review](task-rd02.qmd#rd02-zero-sensitivity) documents the occurrence rationale and modest AIC advantage (0.85) over the redwood constant-zero baseline. Updated integrated means, full-covariance delta intervals, RW/TO Results figure, and four-category supplement table are accepted. Earlier [constant-zero covariance comparisons](task-rd02.qmd#rd02-04) remain distinct from the final selection. Four-site uncertainty, boundary variances, model-selection uncertainty, and unassessed bootstrap coverage remain limitations; formal pairwise treatment contrasts have not been performed.

title: sprout-height display
status: Phase Three complete - display acceptance pending
target: One size/time figure; optional interval-rate companion
summary: The Phase Three analysis selects separate Gaussian(log) year-10 models for a proposed main height figure and retains macro-by-period increment models for supplementary temporal detail. All four chosen models have 2,000 simulated datasets (seed 20261116): both height models have 2,000 usable refits, tanoak increments 1,992, and redwood increments 1,895. Redwood GS–HD height is 4.65 m (basic 95% interval 2.58–6.54 m); HA–HD height and treatment differences in slowing remain uncertain. The joint-height sensitivity, site omissions, covariance boundaries, gradient sensitivity, and Monte Carlo checks qualify model-conditional uncertainty. Predictions weight the four observed sites equally. Main and supplementary displays await human acceptance; RT02, M02, and D02 remain queued.

title: regeneration Results narrative
summary: RD02 is complete with treatment-dependent redwood zero probabilities and constant zeros for the other species categories. Draft a 1–2-page regeneration Results subsection from the updated accepted display and canonical estimates, emphasizing redwood with concise tanoak context and supplemental treatment of other species. Report population-average means and approximate confidence intervals without implying that formal pairwise contrasts have been performed. Every quantitative claim must be traceable to an accepted display or linked table.

title: sprout-height Results narrative
summary: After RD03 acceptance, the proposal is to report redwood and tanoak height/time findings in a distinct 1–1.5-page Results subsection. Combining it with RT01 remains conditional on one shared display and a clearer common message; the narrative must add sprout-development evidence without restating basal-area/density findings. The initial RD03 review is available, but model selection and display acceptance remain pending; later drafting must use the selected tallest-clump estimand and verified contrasts rather than inherited thesis significance language. RD03 Phase Three now supplies model-conditional bootstrap estimates and contrasts, the joint-height sensitivity, and display proposals. Review the Phase Three limitations and obtain display acceptance before drafting manuscript claims; this task remains queued.

title: fuel Results narrative
summary: The fuel Results draft follows the thesis pre-PCT, post-PCT, and vegetation-transition sequence using current publication values. The [source and review decisions](task-rt03.qmd#implemented-source-and-review-decisions) document separated components, integrated means, covariance-aware woody changes, and replacement of inherited significance claims with descriptive rankings. Inline values and the companion table share the canonical CSV; the draft remains pending review, with explicit limits on slash and causal PCT interpretations.

title: study design display
summary: The proposed design display combines study area, treatment layout, and sampling logic if the result remains legible, with the second map or layout moved to the supplement. Its review criterion is that readers can identify the four treatments, replication, and measurement phases without consulting the text.

title: study area and experimental design
summary: Following MD01 acceptance, the proposal retains the setting, four treatments, replication, timing, and PCT context needed to understand the accepted results. A 1–1.5-page Methods subsection and compact design table should make every displayed variable and phase traceable to the experimental design.

title: regeneration and sprout methods
summary: The proposal describes the regeneration and sprout measurements and analyses retained in accepted displays, moving expanded specifications, comparisons, and secondary-species detail to the supplement. The planned 1–1.5-page subsection must make the reported estimands reproducible; it follows RT01/RT02. RD03 now records the thesis-model audit and proposed sensitivities; its sampling target, four-site hierarchy, period definitions, and final prediction target must be resolved before sprout Methods are finalized. RD03 Phase Three now supplies model-conditional bootstrap estimates and contrasts, the joint-height sensitivity, and display proposals. Review the Phase Three limitations and obtain display acceptance before drafting manuscript claims; this task remains queued.

title: fuel methods and estimand
summary: Following RT03, the proposal documents fuel-component definitions, the phase boundary, matched woody contrast, uncertainty/model decisions, and limits on causal interpretation. The planned 1–1.5-page Methods subsection must match the reviewed fuel caption and Results claims, with component/model diagnostics linked through F01 and prediction/inference decisions through RD04.

title: regeneration cohort discussion
summary: The proposed 1.5–2-page discussion interprets redwood and tanoak regeneration under retained overstory as evidence about developing a new cohort in multiaged stands. It tightens the thesis discussion around accepted basal-area/density findings and their uncertainty, with each inference grounded in Results and cited context.

title: sprout development discussion
summary: The proposed sprout discussion connects accepted height patterns to light, retention, and cohort development. Its 1–1.5 pages must explain what the height evidence adds beyond basal area; combining it with D01 depends on whether the reviewed results support one inseparable management message. The initial RD03 review qualifies leader replacement, selected-clump sampling, shade-tolerance interpretation, and the proposed long-term retention threshold; these are limits for later discussion, not accepted new results. RD03 Phase Three now supplies model-conditional bootstrap estimates and contrasts, the joint-height sensitivity, and display proposals. Review the Phase Three limitations and obtain display acceptance before drafting manuscript claims; this task remains queued.

title: fuels and PCT-management discussion
summary: The proposed 1.5–2-page discussion connects phase-specific fuel conditions and the matched woody contrast to silvicultural, fuels, and fire-management questions. It must distinguish potential surface-fuel contribution from directly measured slash and keep interpretation within the reviewed design.

title: limits, integration, and future work
summary: The proposed closing Discussion subsection integrates the limitations governing regeneration and fuel interpretation, then identifies targeted future work. Its 0.5–1-page allocation is intended to resolve caveats from the topical discussions without repeating detailed model results.

title: management problem and study purpose
summary: After Discussion, the proposal condenses the multiaged-silviculture framing into the management problem, study purpose, and scope supported by accepted findings.

title: regeneration and retention context
summary: After Discussion, the proposal retains the sprouting, light, and retention background needed to motivate D01/D02, removing broader context that does not serve the study question.

title: fuels context and questions
summary: The proposal focuses fuel background on phase-specific reference conditions and the PCT question, excluding broad fire-management claims unsupported by the study. Together I01–I03 target a 4–5-page Introduction whose final questions are answered by accepted Results.

title: supplement and machine-readable outputs
summary: The fuel estimates table is accepted for the publication supplement. The remaining inventory is queued: model registries, diagnostics, pairwise comparisons, optional Douglas-fir detail, and machine-readable phase values. The full manuscript also consumes the fuel Results and saved narrative formatter from RT03; refresh that helper before rendering the manuscript.

title: conclusions
summary: After Discussion, the proposal is to write a short conclusion restricted to management implications directly supported by the accepted regeneration, sprout, and fuel results.

title: abstract and title
summary: The proposal drafts the abstract from the accepted Results, Methods, Discussion, and Conclusions, then sets the final title after the abstract stabilizes. This is the last task in the backwards-writing sequence.
